trust_decision.summary: Two string scanners assume that a special character (a backslash escape in the decoder, a newline in the langbind newline-stripper) is always followed by another character, and step the pointer twice; when that character is the last one before the NUL, the loop moves past the terminator and keeps reading the heap.

landing_point.why: The advisory names icalvalue_decode_ical_string. Its backslash branch appends *(p+1) and then does p++ without checking for the NUL.

fix_sites.entry_point: public C API icalvalue_decode_ical_string (src/libical/icalvalue.h:208); glib wrapper i_cal_value_decode_ical_string (src/libical-glib/api/i-cal-value.xml:97-111)
public C API icallangbind_property_eval_string / _r (src/libical/icallangbind_p.h:43-46); Perl XS binding (src/Net-ICal-Libical/netical_wrap.c:1440)
fix_sites.module_kind: language-binding helper (private-named _p file, exported, used by legacy Perl bindings)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/libical/icallangbind_p.c:195-200 (newline-stripping loop in icallangbind_property_eval_string_r; a different loop and trigger character from the decoder named in the advisory)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: icallangbind_p.c is a private-named helper for the old Perl/Python bindings that strips newlines and has nothing to do with escape decoding. The advisory names only icalvalue_decode_ical_string.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what:
An escaped backslash must still decode to one backslash, and a trailing lone escape is dropped without failing the call: "a\" must decode to "a" and return true. In langbind, every newline (including consecutive and trailing ones) is dropped and every other character is kept: "http://a

b
" -> "http://ab". A fix that rejects strings ending in a backslash, or that only adds a NUL check after i++, breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: decoder: string ending in a single backslash
decoder: string ending in an escaped backslash followed by a lone backslash (odd run of trailing backslashes)
langbind: property value ending in a newline
langbind: consecutive newlines (the old loop copied the second newline and skipped the character after it)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: RFC 6868 ^-decoder in icalmemory_append_decoded_string that does p++ after looking at p[1], without first checking p[1] != 0
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same peek-and-skip idiom as the decoder. Today it only advances when p[1] matches a known character; dropping that check would look like a harmless simplification to a maintainer.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: icalparameter_decode_value advances `in` past the escape on any '^' instead of only on a recognised escape
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: An in-place decoder with the same two-step advance. A maintainer adding 'copy unknown escapes verbatim' could easily write it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: vCard dequote loop with the `case 0: p--` step-back removed
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is a second implementation of the iCal dequote at src/libical/icalvalue.c:195-202 in another library (libicalvcard). Both guards are hand-written and easy to lose in a refactor.

O9_family: memory safety: out-of-bounds read past string terminator (CWE-125)

O10_build.toolchain: CMake + C compiler (glib/introspection, Perl and other bindings optional)
O10_build.project_tests: src/test/regression.c test_icalvalue_decode_ical_string (src/test/regression.c:5521-5561) and test_langbind (src/test/regression.c:4352); an ASan build is needed to see the read past the end directly

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a NUL check in the decoder's backslash branch only; or, in langbind, add `if (*i == 0) break;` after the i++, which removes the overread but still lets the second of two consecutive newlines through and skips the character after it.

out_of_scope_notes: src/libical/icalparser.c:388-389 reads *(next - 3) when looking for an escaped comma; the in-code comment says 'HACK may be out of bounds' (possible read before the line start, a different mechanism).
